name: What is a realistic lease-up period for new apartments in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to stabilize a newly built apartment building in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How long does it take to stabilize a newly built apartment building in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lease-up time depends on the size and positioning of the building. A smaller project in a strong submarket may stabilize relatively quickly, while a large luxury development with many similar units may take much longer. Lease-up also depends on whether the building opens into a season with strong renter demand and whether there is competing new supply nearby. In Los Angeles, a realistic plan should include an allowance for concessions, preleasing costs, and slower absorption in the first few months after delivery. Developers and lenders often care just as much about lease-up as they do about construction completion because the project is not truly finished until the building is stabilized. A realistic underwriting model should include a gradual occupancy ramp rather than assuming immediate full rent roll. That protects the project from a cash flow shortfall right after opening.
acceptedAnswer.description: Lease-up can take a few months for a smaller project or much longer for a large luxury building, depending on pricing, amenities, and delivery timing. Many new multifamily projects plan for a lease-up period after completion before reaching stabilized occupancy. Weak positioning or too much competing supply can slow absorption.
